mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and/or Shareholder Registry Extract identifying all shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners of the proposed Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder/UBO jurisdiction of residence or the corporate secretary/registered agent of the holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 (in force for Canada since 11 January 2024) issued by the designated competent authority of the document-origin jurisdiction; where origin jurisdiction is not a Hague Contracting Party, consular legalization through Canadian consular services

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Articles of Association / Constitutional Documents of any corporate shareholder or intermediate holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or notarial authority of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague jurisdictions, consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document copies of all directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners holding 25% or more of the ULC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority / competent government ministry or notary public performing identity verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy certified by a notary public, followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization if required by the receiving Alberta bank, registered agent, or government body

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential and business address for each UBO and director, such as utility bills, bank statements, or registered agent declarations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company, bank, or licensed corporate services provider in the document-origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization with apostille or consular legalization; recent documents preferred to support enhanced due diligence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certified Extract from the corporate register of any foreign corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the foreign jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, signatories, and material counterparties against Canadian sanctions lists issued under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) lists, the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the United States OFAC SDN and Consolidated Sanctions Lists, the United Kingdom HMT Consolidated List, the European Union Consolidated List, and the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified by position, jurisdiction, and connection to the transaction; enhanced due diligence, ongoing monitoring, and independent source verification are applied. All screening must be documented, retained, and made available to FINTRAC and the Alberta corporate registry within applicable statutory timelines.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) through authorized corporate registry agents and the official Alberta corporate access portal at alberta.ca/corporate-registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names in Alberta must contain the distinctive element plus a legal element indicating unlimited liability, e.g. 'Unlimited Liability Corporation,' 'ULC,' 'Société à responsabilité illimitée,' or acceptable abbreviations. Names must be expressed in Roman letters, Arabic numerals, and permitted punctuation. Non-English name components require a certified English or French translation and transliteration for the NUANS search. The name must be distinct from existing Alberta, federal, and registered extra-provincial corporate names, and must not create confusion with protected trademarks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the Director of Corporate Registries, the applicant may file a written request for administrative review with Service Alberta within 30 days of rejection. The request must include the rejection notice, a revised name proposal, a new or updated NUANS report, written consents of any existing corporate or trademark holders if confusion is alleged, and a legal submission distinguishing the proposed name from existing registrations. The Director's final administrative decision may be appealed to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under judicial review principles, service of alternative dispute resolution is optional but recommended, and any further name reservation extension must be obtained before the expiry of the 90-day window or the name must be resubmitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only where the virtual office provider maintains a physical street address in Alberta, is registered as an Alberta corporate registry agent or commercial registered agent, and will accept service of process and regulatory notices. A post-office box or a purely electronic service address is not sufficient under the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate and enhanced for this sector. Quantified risk: approximately 15% annual probability of unannounced registered-office verification or commercial-substance enquiry by Service Alberta, and approximately 25% cumulative probability over three years of a CRA or FINTRAC compliance inspection, given the medium-risk enhanced AML profile of bulk petrochemical polymer wholesale trade and the use of irrevocable letters of credit and swift settlement rails.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), ss 9-27 (incorporation), s 15(2.1) et seq. (unlimited liability corporation election), ss 101-112 (post-incorporation filings); forms prescribed under ABCA regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry - Service Alberta, Government of Alberta; filings are submitted through licensed Authorized Registry Service Providers.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Alberta Business Corporations Act prescribed form) including the unlimited liability shareholder election; Certificate of Incorporation is issued by the Registrar upon filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or blocked-account requirement under Alberta law. A nominal subscription of 100 common shares at CAD 1.00 total is sufficient, and subscribed funds remain freely usable working capital in a Canadian bank account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Corporation subscribes for, and the subscriber is allotted, 100 common shares at CAD 1.00 each, fully paid, constituting initial working capital. (2) The registered office of the Corporation is established at Suite 700, 333 - 7th Avenue SW, Calgary, Alberta, T2P 2Z1, with corporate records kept there. (3) The following officers are appointed: President, Secretary and Treasurer, each to hold office until the next annual meeting, with full banking and contractual signatory authority. (4) The Corporation's by-laws, tabled at this meeting, are adopted, and the fiscal year-end is fixed as December 31. (5) Banking resolutions are approved, authorizing SWIFT LC and irrevocable LC payment transactions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and NUANS Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry - Service Alberta (online portal via licensed Authorized Registry Service Provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a licensed Alberta registry agent to run a Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search (NUANS) for the proposed name, which must include the suffix 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation'. Review the NUANS report for confusing similarity with existing Alberta names. Reserve the approved name for 90 days and retain the reservation certificate for filing.
required_dossiers: Name search instruction sheet with entity type 'ULC'
NUANS search request and bi-weekly search report
Incorporator identification (notarized passport or Canadian provincial photo ID)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusing similarity, submit 2-3 alternate names from the same NUANS report for a new reservation; alternatively reserve a different name or incorporate with a numbered company and later file articles of amendment to adopt a proper name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Authorized Registry Service Provider operating under Service Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation on the prescribed ABCA form, setting out: the ULC unlimited liability clause (ABCA s 15(2.1) et seq.), registered office address in Alberta, 100 common shares without par value, and one or more directors as required by by-law. Execute the articles before a witness, file them electronically or by mail with the statutory fee (approximately CAD 350 electronic filing; CAD 500 paper filing), and retain the registry receipt and file-stamped copy.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation in prescribed ABCA form
NUANS report and name reservation certificate
Consent to act as director(s) and incorporator identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns a query, file amended or corrective articles under ABCA s 10; resolve documentary deficiencies through the registry helpdesk or refile with corrected execution blocks and supplementary declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry - Service Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the articles, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the Alberta corporate registration number and Corporate Access Number (CAN). Verify the legal name, registered office, director particulars and the ULC designation on the certificate; download or order a certified Certificate of Status for banking and counterparty KYC purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For clerical errors in the certificate, apply for a certificate of correction under ABCA s 10; if incorporation is refused, refile corrected articles and address regulatory objections before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Records Book and First Board Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Office of the Corporation; Registrar's statutory filing regime (ABCA ss 19, 101-112)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the board and execute the pro-forma First Board Resolution covering share allotment, registered office adoption, appointment of officers, adoption of by-laws and banking resolutions. Issue share certificates against the subscribed capital, maintain the minute book and securities register at the registered office, and file any required Notice of Registered Office or Notice of Directors within 15 days of the relevant change.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (adopted by the incorporating director)
By-law No. 1 (governance, meetings, officers, banking, indemnity)
Minute book and corporate seal (if adopted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notices are filed late, file the statutory notice immediately and pay the applicable late-filing fee; cure any governance omissions by unanimous board consent resolution and update the corporate records retroactively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Activation with Municipal Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Number and tax accounts); City of Calgary or City of Edmonton business licence and building/fire approval offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the CRA for a Business Number, GST/HST account and Alberta corporate tax account using the Certificate of Incorporation. Where an office or warehouse is operated, obtain the municipal business licence, occupancy permit, Alberta Fire Code inspection and OHS clearance as applicable. Open the corporate bank account using the certificate, by-laws, board resolutions and officer identification; configure SWIFT LC and irrevocable LC payment rails for the petrochemical trading operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Access Number
First Board Resolution and banking resolution
Officer passports and corporate minute book
Lease or registered office address proof and municipal licence application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA registration is delayed beyond 5 business days, escalate via CRA business registry; if a municipal licence or fire inspection is refused, resubmit with corrected floor plans and occupancy documentation or appeal through the municipal business licence appeal committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to pure wholesale trading of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules; where warehousing or distribution centres are operated, authority lies with municipal planning and development departments (City of Calgary/City of Edmonton) and Alberta Municipal Affairs for fire and building code compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence with warehouse condition and Fire Safety Inspection Certificate; no separate Alberta industrial operating permit is imposed on ISIC 4669 / NAICS 424690 wholesale merchant activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA), Government of Alberta
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - wholesale distribution and enclosed warehousing of finished polymer granules is not a Schedule 1 'Activity' under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA), RSA 2000 c E-12; mandatory EIA filing threshold is not triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater or volatile organic compound (VOC) discharge permit required for trading operations; pellet and dust containment measures must prevent fugitive emissions beyond site boundaries; stormwater discharges managed under municipal drainage by-laws; polymer packaging and scrap disposal must meet the Alberta Recycling Regulation; if stationary unloading or conveying equipment is installed, particulate emissions should remain below Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives (PM10 guideline) and visible dust must not cross the property boundary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Alberta Fire Code inspection and fire safety certification covering extinguishing systems, egress and hazardous storage limits; Alberta OHS clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000 c O-8 and the OHS Code including workplace hazard assessment and chemical safety training; structural load certification for racked or stacked 25 kg granule bags; municipal occupancy permit for the commercial office and warehouse premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - My Business Account portal; Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA under a tax collection agreement with the Province of Alberta.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Alberta ULC, apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) using form RC1, either through the CRA's 'Register a Business with CRA' online service or by mail/fax. The same BN is used to enroll for GST/HST, payroll deductions, corporate income tax, and Alberta provincial corporate income tax. Non-resident ULCs must provide information regarding Canadian directors and place of business; a Canadian resident agent may be required for service. Registration for GST/HST is mandatory immediately if the entity makes taxable supplies in Canada and is not a small supplier, or if it solicits business in Canada; otherwise registration may be voluntary to claim input tax credits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The Alberta ULC is taxed as a corporation under the Canadian Income Tax Act; no Canadian 'check-the-box' or entity classification election exists for ULCs. For U.S. federal tax purposes only, the ULC may be treated as a disregarded entity or partnership if the owner files a Form 8832/late check-the-box election, but such U.S. classification does not alter Canadian CRA entity-level taxation. No hybrid mismatch election is available under Canadian domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST); Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax or HST component
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies in the last four consecutive calendar quarters (or in a single calendar quarter for a new business), unless the entity is a tax-recovery registrant or is already required to register due to non-resident solicitation. Charities and public institutions have a CAD 50,000 threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government pre-clearance of invoices exists in Canada. GST/HST registrants must issue a valid tax invoice containing prescribed information (supplier name, BN, GST registration number, taxable supplies, tax rate and amount). The CRA requires electronic records to be retained in a readable format for six years and may perform real-time access audits to assess evidence of export.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of virgin polyethylene/polypropylene granules is zero-rated as a commercial product if the supplier transfers possession or ownership of the goods to a non-resident and the goods are shipped by the supplier or by the non-resident purchaser to a destination outside Canada, or exported under CRA-approved export programs for distribution. The supplier must retain contemporaneous evidence showing that the goods were actually delivered outside Canada within the required time and not subsequently consumed in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration submitted electronically through CBSA eManifest / Canadian Export Reporting System (SES)
Bill of Lading or other shipping document evidencing export from Canada
Proof of settlement / foreign currency receipt (SWIFT MT103, bank advice) where the sale price is in USD
Cargo or container tracking report showing arrival at foreign port
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may disallow any zero-rating claim and reassess GST at 5% if the exporter cannot provide sufficient documentary proof of export; interest and penalties apply from the original filing date. Knowingly making false statements with intent to evade tax under the Excise Tax Act may attract civil penalties of up to 25% of the tax sought, and tax evasion charges can lead to fines of up to 200% of the tax avoided and imprisonment. Exporters should maintain a six-year documentary retention period to mitigate clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange surveillance and integrity oversight are shared with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada maintains no dedicated foreign exchange administration and imposes no exchange control licensing regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar and foreign currencies are fully convertible on both current and capital account. Canada adheres to IMF Article VIII obligations. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted; the only compliance hurdles are Canadian withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (subject to treaty relief) and standard corporate documentation supporting the distribution. There is no requirement for ministerial FX approval or evidence of genuine trade for conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not mandate surrender, conversion, repatriation, or minimum holding timelines for export receipts. A ULC may retain export proceeds in foreign currency. Cross-border currency and monetary instrument movement in excess of CAD 10,000 must be reported to the Canada Border Services Agency / FINTRAC, otherwise no statutory conversion ratio or surrender timeline exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Treasury Account, USD and CAD clearing, SWIFT/LC desk
Operational Account with cross-border wire and foreign exchange facilities
Trade Finance Operating Account and Commercial LC issuance desk
Capital Escrow Account for inbound equity injection and treasury operations
Operational Account with USD sweep and EDD banking support

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low. A non-resident or unlicensed electronic money institution cannot serve as a primary treasury rail for this ULC because it lacks Canadian MSB registration under FINTRAC, Retail Payment Activities Act licensing, SWIFT correspondent access, LC issuance powers, and LVTS clearing membership. Canadian-licensed fintech platforms may support secondary expense payments, but for bulk petrochemical polymer settlements and documentary credits, Tier 1 bank rails remain legally and operationally necessary.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance at a Canadian branch is not a universal statutory requirement, but most Tier 1 banks mandate a live video interview with original, notarized Alberta Registry documents for non-resident directors and shareholders of a ULC. Given the unlimited liability structure and non-resident ownership, an in-person or embassy-notarized meeting may be requested under enhanced due diligence. Fully remote online-only onboarding is generally unavailable for this medium-risk, non-resident-controlled wholesale trade entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC unlimited liability structure perceived as opaque or hybrid tax-transparent vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of Alberta incorporation certificate, Alberta Corporate Registry continuous search report, shareholders agreement, unlimited liability explanation letter, Canadian legal opinion on ULC characteristics, directors' resolution, notarized passports, proof of residential address, and source-of-wealth statements for all 25%+ shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bulk petrochemical polymer wholesale sector flagged as high-value trade with potential dual-use concern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial supply agreements with reputable counterparties, pro-forma invoices, bill-of-lading samples, ISO 9001 quality certificates, safety data sheets, insurance certificate, end-user attestation, sanctions screening results, and trade compliance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment flows routed through intermediate jurisdictions or third-country treasury centers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organizational chart, full beneficial-ownership chain, funding source declaration, board-approved treasury routing policy, explanation of intermediary bank purposes, bank statements of intermediate entities, and supporting commercial contracts for each leg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large turnover relative to established operating history triggering financial crime escalation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 24-month cash flow forecast, audited parent-company financial statements, board-approved working capital policy, warehouse storage or third-party logistics agreements, evidence of physical polymer offtake, and transaction-specific business rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export-control exposure from international polymer suppliers and buyers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening program, counterparty OFAC screening certificates, export permit due diligence (where applicable), country of origin paperwork, plastic polymers end-use assurance, and negative media and PEP review.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections must be wired to the ULC Alberta operating account in CAD, USD, or EUR via SWIFT MT103 with payment narrative 'ULC share subscription – capital contribution'. Canada does not assign statutory FX purpose codes; the receiving Canadian bank maps the payment under the Statistics Canada Balance of Payments direct investment equity category for reports exceeding the applicable threshold (commonly CAD 1,000,000). The verification pack must include: board resolution authorizing share issuance, executed subscription agreement, share register update, Alberta corporate allotment filing, director resolution opening the bank account, source-of-funds documentation for every transferring shareholder, and sanctions clearances. Settlement should clear through Payments Canada LVTS for CAD, via the Canadian bank's correspondent network for USD over CHIPS/Fedwire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For polymer imports, disbursements should be executed through irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued according to UCP600 via SWIFT MT700, with settlement made by SWIFT MT103/202 upon presentation of conforming documents. Open-account CAD payments should clear through LVTS; USD payments should clear through the Canadian bank's US correspondent using Fedwire or CHIPS. Payment memos must carry the LC number and commercial invoice reference. No foreign currency surrender or conversion is required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards up to 24 months with a Schedule I Canadian chartered bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic or restricted currencies outside the Canadian domestic deliverable market
Cross-currency interest rate swaps between CAD, USD, and EUR for matched treasury risk
Vanilla FX options for capped downside protection
Exchange-traded futures and options on CME or ICE for USD/CAD and EUR/USD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or the previous annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to $200 per day; administrative strike-off possible after 90 days of non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if the corporation has more than 10 members and gross revenue for the financial year exceeds $500,000

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation required; register of beneficial owners must be updated upon any change in shareholdings or control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% aggregate (15% federal general corporate rate + 8% Alberta provincial rate; federal rate net of provincial abatement)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays; available incentives include federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) refundable investment tax credits, accelerated capital cost allowance under the Accelerated Investment Incentive, and Alberta's flat 8% rate. A ULC controlled by non-residents does not qualify for the Small Business Deduction and therefore applies the full 23% combined rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Alberta Schedule 5 – Provincial Tax Calculation). Filed via CRA EFILE / TELEFILE / My Business Account; mandatory electronic filing for gross revenue exceeding CAD 1 million.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year as chosen in the first taxation year; usually calendar-year if no election)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due within 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance of tax due within 2 months after fiscal year-end (3 months for Canadian-controlled private corporations eligible for the owner-manager remuneration exception). Alberta does not require a separate provincial corporate return; the T2 federal return is used for provincial purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter legal name, CRA 9-digit business number, registered Alberta office address, fiscal year-end, and the corporation's status (Alberta ULC, unlimited liability corporation).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a ULC with non-resident shareholders, use the Canadian registered office address; identify the foreign ultimate parent in Schedule 3 (Foreign Income Tax) or in the 'type of corporation' table. The corporation is a Canadian resident because it is incorporated in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross sales of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules, including all wholesale trading revenue, commissions, freight recovered, and ancillary charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All worldwide income of the Canadian-resident corporation is reportable; the non-resident parent's relationship does not exempt revenue. For cross-border purchases, apply arm's length prices on the same return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct cost of goods sold, logistics, taxes, salaries, interest on debt, depreciation, and business expenses relevant to petrochemical distribution.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses charged from non-resident affiliates must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; cross-border charges for management fees and royalties require CRA Form T106 and Part XIII withholding if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate Alberta corporate income tax at 8% on taxable income allocated to Alberta using the permanent establishment rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the ULC is considered a permanent establishment of a non-resident group, file Schedule 5 with allocation fractions based on sales and gross property in Alberta; maintain PE payroll and office substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay up to 12 months; late-payment interest compounded daily at the prescribed rate (CRA rates, currently around 9% but variable). Gross negligence penalties equal to 50% of the understated amount are assessed under s. 163(2).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII of the Income Tax Act) on dividends paid to non-residents, unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Canadian payor may withhold at a reduced treaty rate only after receiving a completed Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits under a Tax Convention) from the final recipient. The foreign shareholder must be the beneficial owner and provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) upon CRA request. For a US parent corporation owning at least 10% of voting shares, the reduced rate is 5%; otherwise 15% for portfolio dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory source rate: royalties 25%, interest 25%. Under the Canada-US tax treaty, arm's-length interest is generally 0% and industrial royalties (patents, trade secrets, etc.) may be 0%; complex limitation-on-benefits rules apply. Late remittance penalties are 10% plus daily interest under Regulation 100.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No mandatory local file threshold is prescribed by statute; however, CRA requires contemporaneous documentation to be available for any non-arm's-length cross-border transaction. Penalty risk begins when the net transfer pricing adjustment exceeds the lesser of CAD 5 million or 10% of gross revenue; a Master File and Country-by-Country Report are mandatory for MNE groups with consolidated revenue of CAD 1 billion or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as in certain offshore jurisdictions. The CRA uses the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under s. 245 to disregard transactions without genuine business purpose, and treaty benefits require the ULC to have real officers, offices, bank accounts, and commercial decisions in Alberta.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – False Invoicing & Revenue Concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully underreporting gross revenue from wholesale polymer sales, issuing fictitious purchase invoices from related shell suppliers, or transferring trading income to non-resident affiliates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Income Tax Act s. 239(2) (evasion), max fine of CAD 100,000 and up to 5 years imprisonment (indictable); summary conviction fine of CAD 25,000 to CAD 100,000 and up to 2 years imprisonment. Civil penalties include gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax plus compound interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable under s. 227.1 for withheld source deductions; if they directed or participated in the fraudulent scheme, they may be jointly and severally liable for the full corporate tax arrears, face asset seizure orders, travel bans, and criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Export Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Importing polyethylene or polypropylene granules from a related non-resident refiner at an artificially inflated price while failing to maintain a benchmark comparable analysis; also charging excessive management fees from offshore shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA recharacterizes the margin under s. 247(2); a transfer pricing penalty of 10% of the gross adjustment applies if the net adjustment exceeds the threshold (lesser of CAD 5 million or 10% gross revenue). Interest and gross negligence penalties can be applied concurrently.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knew or authorized the mispricing are subject to a penalty of 10% of the adjustment under s. 247.3, and can be named as third parties in proceedings with asset freezes; criminal referral may follow if documentation was fabricating.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a mailbox ULC with minimal business activity, no Alberta employees or warehouse, and routing intercompany payments exclusively to claim Canada-US treaty relief without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR (s. 245) denies the transaction benefit: dividends may be recharacterized as taxable paid-up capital, treaty benefits denied, and Part XIII WHT is reassessed at 25%; a GAAR penalty of 50% of the tax benefit applies. The entity may also be de-listed as a resident for DTA purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for gross negligence penalties if they caused the entity to advance the sham structure; CRA may extend liability to personal assets, including bank accounts and real estate, and issue a certificate of arrest for travel outside Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML & Payment Fanning via Trade Finance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Swift LC and irrevocable LC payment rails to move funds between related entities without reporting large or suspicious transactions under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to report suspicious transactions can trigger fines up to CAD 1 million for individuals and CAD 5 million for financial entities, per FINTRAC and Financial Institution Statutes. For a medium-risk petrochemical trader, false structuring and trade-based money laundering may attract additional criminal charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can be personally fined or sentenced for misrepresentation to FINTRAC; personal liability extends to civil forfeiture proceedings under the Alberta Civil Forfeiture Act if the funds originated from criminal activity.
